source.title: Pumpout: A Meta Approach for Robustly Training Deep Neural Networks with Noisy Labels
source.authors: Bo Han; Gang Niu; Jiangchao Yao; Xing-Rui Yu; Miao Xu; I. Tsang; Masashi Sugiyama

page_placements.theme: Memorization and label-corruption outcomes depend on mechanism

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, including appendix material. It contains some OCR-like symbol substitutions, but the reported experimental outcomes are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how over-parameterized networks memorize noisy labels and how training interventions affect test accuracy in noisy-label learning, a related setting to the claim's natural-label generalization topic.
record.gate_note: The paper directly reports memorization and test accuracy under heavy label noise, and separately evaluates methods that selectively forget or counter-train on examples. It does not test most claim versions' specified natural-label settings. Cited findings, including Zhang et al. (2017), are not treated as this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study uses noisy-label memorization to motivate and evaluate SIGUA. It does not compare fitting fully random labels with generalizing on natural labels under the same training recipe, as V1 requires. Its forgetting interventions and noisy-label benchmark comparisons do not test any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that distinguishing desired from undesired memorization lets SIGUA improve self-teaching and backward correction, with improvements often statistically significant in their proof-of-concept noisy-label experiments.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates noisy-label learning with sample selection and corrected losses, including selective gradient ascent, rather than the claim's fixed-random-label versus natural-label standard-training comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by noise type (symmetry versus pair and open-set), dataset, learning method, and architecture; the authors report differences between SIGUASL and SIGUABC across noise conditions and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Both MNIST networks fit all training examples with 80% label corruption before intervention. Oracle SIGUA subsequently erased 99% of flipped-label memorization and raised clean-test accuracy from 23% to 95%; StopGrad produced smaller gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selectively counter-training on known corrupted labels can improve clean-test accuracy after noisy-label memorization.

fits_no_version.finding: SIGUA and its comparators are evaluated for clean-test accuracy under open-set noise; replacing the standard CNN with ResNet-18 also improves SIGUA's noisy-label benchmark accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noisy-label robustness depends on the learning method and architecture.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 119, 2020
record.problems: The motivating Figure 1 experiment uses true labels to identify flipped examples; the main experiments are described as proof-of-concept and exclude data augmentation. Figure-based accuracy curves do not provide exact values or numeric standard deviations in the supplied text. Table 1 reports no standard deviations.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports many separate accuracy curves across datasets, methods, and noise regimes in Figures 2–5 and tables in Appendix B. Those numerous figure-only conditions were not extracted because they do not test the claim's specified natural-label generalization setting; the retained rows capture the direct memorization/test-accuracy motivating experiment and representative numeric benchmark outcomes.

untested.parts: No matched comparison of fully random-label fitting, chance-level random-label test accuracy, and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and training recipe. The 80% noise experiment retains label signal.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error. The reported epoch-wise double descent concerns training duration.
No controlled image-classification comparison between convolutional and fully connected architectures or manipulation of local connectivity.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison under matched tuning.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No dropout ablation; including dropout in an architecture does not measure its effect.
No magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No influence-based identification and removal of highly memorized examples, retraining, or matched random-removal control. Counter-training on corrupted labels measures a different intervention.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Its own memorization results concern partially corrupted labels; the fully random-label finding is attributed to Zhang et al. Benchmark comparisons remain useful study results but provide no verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Tests memorization of heavily corrupted labels and clean-test accuracy, but not fitting fixed random labels versus natural labels under the specified standard-training recipes; no Inception, AlexNet or MLP settings.

rows.subject: wide network, 784-[Lin(10k)-BN-ReLU]-[Lin(100)-BN-ReLU]-Lin(10)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with 80% symmetric label noise using standard training through epoch 150, then StopGrad on intact data.

conditions.value: momentum SGD; learning rate 0.01 and momentum 0.9 fixed

rows.measure: training accuracy on flipped examples; test accuracy on label-noise-free test data
rows.baseline: At the end of training before StopGrad, test accuracy 23%.
rows.value: At the end of training, StopGrad made the network forget 5% of flipped data; test accuracy improved from 23% to 59%.
rows.uncertainty: means with standard deviations over 5 repeats are plotted; numeric standard deviations not stated
rows.note: The paper says both networks memorized all data before the intervention. This row records the reported StopGrad outcome; it concerns corrupted-label training rather than the version's natural-label setup.
rows.check: The 5% forgetting and 23% to 59% test-accuracy change are correctly reported, but measure an oracle intervention after 80%-corrupted-label training. StopGrad ignores flipped examples and continues descent on intact examples. These outcomes do not establish V1; separate forgetting and test accuracy if retaining these results.
